Definition: of Chaldee origin (compare H2924); the fresh, i.e. young girl; talitha (O maiden):--talitha.
BiblicalUsage: Jesus takes the dead girl by the hand and says, Talitha cumi, which is, being interpreted, Damsel, I say unto thee, arise. The word is Aramaic, not Greek: talitha, little girl, fresh and young. Mark keeps the sound of Jesus' own words, and then gives the meaning for readers who did not know Aramaic.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Mark kept the Aramaic because the moment was too personal to translate away: Jesus speaks to the girl by name, and she gets up.
